cards.q: What does AAA stand for and what do the three functions control?
cards.a: Authentication (who are you?), Authorization (what are you allowed to do?), and Accounting (what did you do?).

cards.q: What command enables the IOS AAA framework?
cards.a: aaa new-model

cards.q: What are the three major components that AAA is built around?
cards.a: aaa new-model, AAA method lists, and AAA services such as authentication, authorization, and accounting.

cards.q: What does the 'aaa authentication login default group tacacs+ local' command do, and in what order?
cards.a: It attempts TACACS+ authentication first and uses the local database as a fallback when the TACACS+ method is unavailable according to AAA fallback rules.

cards.q: What can AAA authorization control?
cards.a: EXEC access, commands, network services, privilege levels, and other supported IOS services.

cards.q: Does accounting grant or deny access?
cards.a: No. Accounting records activity for auditing and tracking but never grants or denies access.

cards.q: Why must you verify management-access fallback after enabling aaa new-model?
cards.a: Enabling aaa new-model can change existing line authentication behavior; a pre-existing 'login local' does not automatically replace a newly configured AAA method list, so you must verify effective config and fallback before testing remote access.

cards.q: What is a AAA method list?
cards.a: It defines how IOS performs a particular AAA operation, including the methods and their order of use.

cards.q: What does 'commands N' in 'aaa authorization commands N' mean?
cards.a: It refers to the IOS privilege level N, NOT the number of commands. For example, commands 15 controls commands executed at privilege level 15.

cards.q: How does a named method list differ from the default method list?
cards.a: The default list is used automatically when no named list is specified for a service; a named list must be explicitly applied (e.g., with 'login authentication VTY-AUTH').

cards.q: With 'aaa authentication login default group tacacs+ local', when does fallback to local occur?
cards.a: Fallback to local occurs when the TACACS+ method is unavailable or times out according to AAA fallback rules; a definitive authentication rejection from the server generally does not trigger local fallback.

cards.q: Why does an explicit AAA server rejection not automatically fall back to the next method?
cards.a: AAA distinguishes a definitive authentication rejection (which should not be bypassed) from a server timeout/unavailability, so a central server's explicit denial is not accidentally bypassed by local authentication.

cards.q: What is TACACS+ transport and ports, compared to RADIUS?
cards.a: TACACS+ uses TCP port 49 for both authentication and accounting; RADIUS uses UDP 1812 for authentication and UDP 1813 for accounting.

cards.q: Why is TACACS+ commonly preferred for network-device administrative access?
cards.a: Because it provides strong separation of authentication and authorization and supports granular command authorization.

cards.q: How do TACACS+ and RADIUS differ in encryption of AAA data?
cards.a: TACACS+ encrypts the AAA packet body; RADIUS traditionally encrypts only the password field (though modern deployments vary).

cards.q: What command creates a local user with privilege 15 and a secret?
cards.a: username admin privilege 15 secret StrongPassword

cards.q: What is the difference between EXEC authorization and command authorization?
cards.a: EXEC authorization controls whether a user can obtain an EXEC shell; command authorization controls which commands a user can run, based on privilege level.

cards.q: What privilege levels are commonly used in Cisco IOS?
cards.a: Level 0 (very limited commands), level 1 (user EXEC), and level 15 (privileged EXEC).

cards.q: What are the common accounting keywords and their meanings?
cards.a: start-stop (send start and stop records), stop-only (send only stop records), and none (no accounting).

cards.q: What does 'aaa authorization network' control?
cards.a: Network-service authorization relevant to network-access services such as supported PPP/VPN-related AAA functions.

cards.q: Why is authentication success not automatically authorization success?
cards.a: Authentication and authorization are separate AAA functions; a user can authenticate successfully yet still fail authorization, so troubleshooting must check both separately.

cards.q: What is the difference between 'login', 'login local', and 'login authentication <method-list>'?
cards.a: 'login' uses the line password, 'login local' uses the local username database, and 'login authentication <method-list>' uses the specified AAA method list; they are not interchangeable.

cards.q: Why is a local user database required for a 'local' AAA fallback?
cards.a: The 'local' method references the local username database; without an existing username it cannot authenticate, so a local fallback is not useful unless local users exist.

cards.q: What command verifies AAA server status and configuration?
cards.a: show aaa servers, and show aaa sessions to view AAA sessions; show running-config | section aaa shows the AAA configuration.

cards.q: What command tests AAA authentication against a TACACS+ group?
cards.a: test aaa group tacacs+ username password legacy (exact syntax varies by IOS/platform).

cards.q: What debug commands are used to troubleshoot AAA authentication, authorization, and accounting?
cards.a: debug aaa authentication, debug aaa authorization, and debug aaa accounting; additionally debug tacacs and debug radius for the respective protocols.

cards.q: What ordering is used when troubleshooting failing AAA?
cards.a: Check AAA config, then reachability to the server, then the server group, then shared secret, then authentication, then EXEC authorization, then command authorization, then accounting.

cards.q: What are the best practices to avoid AAA lockout on a remote device?
cards.a: Keep an existing admin session open, configure the new AAA method with a local fallback and emergency account, open a second test session, test authentication/authorization/accounting, and only then close the original session; maintain console/OOB access.

cards.q: What are the legacy RADIUS ports versus modern ports?
cards.a: Legacy RADIUS used UDP 1645 (auth) and UDP 1646 (accounting); modern deployments use UDP 1812 (auth) and UDP 1813 (accounting).

cards.q: Identify which of the following is a named method list: 'aaa authentication login default group tacacs+ local' or 'aaa authentication login VTY-AUTH group tacacs+ local'?
cards.a: The VTY-AUTH one is a named method list (it must be explicitly applied); 'default' is the default method list used automatically when no named list is specified.

cards.q: What is the overall role of AAA on a Cisco device?
cards.a: AAA is a policy framework combining authentication, authorization, and accounting, built with aaa new-model, method lists, and services, using local or centralized TACACS+/RADIUS servers.

cards.q: What does 'aaa authorization commands 15 default group tacacs+ local' control?
cards.a: It authorizes commands executed at privilege level 15, using TACACS+ first with local fallback according to AAA rules.
